summary:
AstroSuit is a student-built prototype of a health-monitoring suit for astronauts on space missions. We built a foil-insulated suit model with an Arduino and sensors for gas, temperature, humidity, distance, and touch. The Arduino compares readings with configured thresholds and shows a simple status cue: a green LED for the normal range and a red LED when a threshold is crossed.

This addresses the challenge by bringing a few in-suit readings and a clear status signal together in one place, so changes are easier to notice when an astronaut is far from immediate medical support. Spaceflight health is shaped by five NASA hazard groups; our prototype covers only selected sensor readings and does not measure all of them.

It matters because astronauts on distant missions cannot rely on immediate medical support. Next, we will calibrate the sensors, test the alert logic, add a digital display, and evaluate a NASA crew-physiology dataset. AstroSuit is an educational prototype, not a medical device.
details:
What it does and how it works
AstroSuit is a physical prototype that brings a few in-suit readings together with a clear status cue. An Arduino reads a gas sensor, a temperature and humidity sensor, an ultrasonic distance sensor, and a touch input. It compares the readings with configured thresholds and lights a green LED for the normal range or a red LED when a threshold is crossed.

Benefits and intended impact
Small changes can be harder to notice when an astronaut is far from immediate medical support. AstroSuit makes selected environmental signals easier to see and gives a simple local alert. It is an awareness tool and an educational prototype, not a medical device.

Tools and hardware
Foil-insulated suit model, Arduino board, gas sensor, temperature and humidity sensor, ultrasonic sensor, touch sensor, and green/red LEDs. Programming: [ADD LANGUAGE/IDE, e.g. Arduino C++ in Arduino IDE].

Creativity
We combined several low-cost sensors and a simple two-color status cue on a wearable suit model, so a reading becomes a signal that can be understood at a glance.

Factors we considered
NASA identifies five hazard groups of spaceflight; our prototype addresses only selected sensor readings and does not measure all five. The gas sensor’s target gas and the thresholds still need calibration and documentation. A fan would reduce visor fog but does not remove CO₂. AI or face-based cues would need consent, privacy safeguards, and testing.

Current status and next steps
The suit model, electronics, sensors, and LED status are built. We have not yet calibrated the sensors or tested the alert logic. Next, we will calibrate the sensors, add a digital display, test fog airflow safely, and evaluate a NASA crew-physiology dataset.
